items.title: [Dependencies] Remove unused packages and review dependency footprint
items.body:
## Description
The package manifest includes dependencies named `fs` (`^0.0.1-security`), `path`, `patch`, and `vercel`. The inspected source imports the Node.js built-in filesystem and path modules, while no direct use of the `patch` package was identified in the repository tree. Unneeded packages increase installation size and supply-chain surface.

## Objective
Keep runtime and build dependencies minimal and intentional.

## Scope
- Confirm actual usage of every direct dependency across build and deployment configuration.
- Remove packages that are unused or shadow Node.js built-ins, where safe.
- Retain dependencies required by the configured Vercel build.
- Review the resulting lockfile and document any package kept for deployment reasons.
- Do not perform broad dependency upgrades as part of this cleanup unless separately justified.

## Acceptance criteria
- Each direct dependency has a documented or verifiable use.
- Unused packages are removed from both `package.json` and the lockfile.
- `npm ci` and the production build succeed after the cleanup.
- Deployment behavior remains unchanged.

items.title: Remove unused packages and track the npm audit findings
items.body:
Left open by the 2026-10-12 security audit (see #23).

**Packages with no imports under `src/`**

`@expo/ui`, `expo-device`, `expo-glass-effect`, `expo-symbols`, `expo-font`.

These look left over from the Expo template. They were not removed during the audit because removing a native package needs the app to be run afterwards on a phone and on web to confirm nothing depended on it indirectly (`expo-font`, for example, can be needed by icon sets).

- [ ] Remove them one at a time, running the app on web and in Expo Go after each.
- [ ] `@testing-library/jest-native` is deprecated (its matchers are built into `@testing-library/react-native` now) and `ts-jest` may be unused; check on `unitTests`.

**`npm audit`**

66 findings on 2026-10-12: none critical, 50 high, 16 moderate. Almost all are in build and test tooling (jest, metro, `node-forge`, `braces`, `js-yaml`) that never reaches a player's device. The fixes npm offers are downgrades to years-old majors such as `expo@44`, so there is nothing sensible to apply today.

The one that ships in the app is `decode-uri-component` under `expo-router`: a badly formed link could make the app hang while decoding it. It needs someone to open a crafted link on purpose.

- [ ] Re-run `npm audit` after each Expo SDK upgrade and note what clears.

items.title: Dependencies and SDK: per-TFM Microsoft.Extensions versions, remove unused packages, pin SDK in global.json

milestone.description: Improvements after 3.0.0: CI/CD, tests, analyzers, AOT, infrastructure. No breaking changes.

items.body:
## Dependencies
- All `Microsoft.Extensions.*` references are 10.0.x for every TFM. net8.0 consumers (for example ASP.NET Core 8 apps) get 10.x packages forced into their graph. For a library it is usual to reference the lowest supported version per TFM (8.0.x for net8.0, 9.0.x for net9.0, 10.0.x for net10.0), or 8.0.x for all.
- `Sigil` is referenced but not used in our code (it is there for Genius.NET -> Jil). Goes away together with Genius.NET (see the Genius issue).
- `MusixmatchClientLib` pulls GraphQL.Client, System.Reactive, Newtonsoft.Json (see the Musixmatch issue).
- No vulnerable packages (`dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive`). Minor updates available: Microsoft.Extensions.* 10.0.14, HtmlAgilityPack 1.13.1, xunit.v3 4.0.2, xunit.runner.visualstudio 4.0.1, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk 18.11.0, Microsoft.Testing.Extensions.CodeCoverage 18.12.0.
- No `Directory.Packages.props`: FakeItEasy, xunit, test SDK versions are repeated in three csproj files. Central Package Management would keep them in one place.

## SDK / language
- `LangVersion latest` with SDK 10 is C# 14, and the code already uses a C# 14 feature (null-conditional assignment `Options?.Enabled = true` in `ExternalProviderBase`). `global.json` has no `sdk` section, so on a machine with only SDK 8/9 the build fails with a confusing error. Add `"sdk": { "version": "10.0.100", "rollForward": "latestFeature" }`.
- CS8618 warnings on every build: `ExternalProviderBase.Parser`, `ExternalProviderBase.WebClient`, `MusixmatchOptions.ApiKey`.

items.title: [P1][Security] Triage dependency advisories and remove unused packages before store release
items.body:
## Measured evidence
npm audit against the committed package-lock.json on 2026-09-27 reports 27 affected dependency entries: 2 critical, 13 high, 10 moderate, 2 low. These counts are dependency entries, not 27 independently exploitable production vulnerabilities.

Critical entries: jspdf (direct), tar (transitive). High entries include fast-xml-parser, lodash, vite, rollup and postcss. The source search found no active src/ or Worker imports for jspdf, react-quill, lodash or fast-xml-parser; confirm transitive/build use before removal. Runtime, build-time and unused-package reachability must be separated.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Preserve a dated audit/SBOM and inspect advisory IDs, affected lockfile versions, runtime reachability and fixed ranges.
- [ ] Remove unused dependencies and update required packages in bounded changes.
- [ ] Do not apply npm audit fix --force blindly (react-quill suggestion includes a major/downgrade-like change).
- [ ] Revalidate the @capgo native-audio patch against the resolved version and native playback behavior.
- [ ] Run tests/lint/build and exact release-binary checks after updates; track residual advisories with justification.
- [ ] Add routine dependency monitoring and review lockfile updates.

Priority P1 security triage; effort M, remediation depends on reachability. No packages or lockfile were changed by this audit.

## Audit provenance
Read-only source audit on 2026-09-27 at `489ffc54f5ad76b7d71a359684f80c1921628b00` (Voxyl 0.4.5). No application source, deployment or production data was changed. Static findings are distinguished from runtime/device validation.
